Subject: Pilot billing question — long context sessions and invoice line mapping

Hi Karthik,

Thanks again for running the POC last week. We have a couple of billing questions from our finance team as we prepare the internal purchase request:

- For sessions where we maintain a 40k token context window (multiple shorter user queries appended to the same conversation), how will those be split on the invoice? Do you bill per call or per aggregated conversation window?
- We saw a line item in the sample usage that looked like several small session charges instead of one aggregated charge — why would that happen?
- Are KV cache hits/continuous prefix reuse credited back to reduce tokenable charges? Our model keeps a warm prefix for 3–4 hours across calls.

Would appreciate a short, concrete mapping we can give procurement (sample invoice lines helpful).

Hi Sarah — thanks for the clear questions. High level answers below; Ben and Marissa are cc'd with more details + a sample invoice breakdown.

1) Aggregation vs per-call: By default our hosted billing aggregates tokens by conversational session when the requests are pinned to the same conversation id (we call this a conversation window). However there are two ways we end up with multiple invoice lines for what looks like the same logical session:
   - If calls come from different API keys or different pinned model versions they are treated as separate billable entities and appear as separate invoice lines.
   - If the session's context exceeds the configured rolling window and is split by the runtime (we split for memory/throughput reasons), those splits are billed as distinct tokens for each resulting service call.

2) Small session charges: that typically happens when short-lived sessions are not using conversation pinning or when streaming responses are counted as multiple per-call buckets (small bursts).

3) KV cache/prefix crediting: We do give credits for re-used prefixes via our KV cache crediting policy — but credits are applied as a post-processing line item (invoice credit) and are bounded by a minimum recomputation threshold. Ben will add an example chart.

I'll keep this short so Marissa/Ben can add the sample invoice lines.

Thanks,
Karthik

Hi Sarah,

Adding the technical/billing mapping here and an attached quick chart. Key points: 

- Conversation windowing: If your integration sends a stable conversation_id on each request, we aggregate tokens into a single conversation bucket and bill once per invoice period for that bucket. If conversation_id changes (or API key changes), we split the token accounting.

- Session splitting: The runtime may split a >32k token context into two execution calls (backend optimization). Each execution call produces a billable token count. Example: 45k context -> backend does 30k + 15k calls -> invoice shows two billed calls. We attach a sample where we re-map those two calls to a single logical invoice line for clarity (see sample_invoice_lines.pdf).

- Rounding and minimums: We meter tokens at 1-token granularity then round invoice lines to the nearest billing quantum (our pilot uses a 10-token quantum for hosted accounts). We only apply minimum per-conversation floor for low-traffic customers — enterprise commits override floors with custom units.

- KV cache credits: We calculate prefix reuse over a rolling 24-hour window. Credit = min(reused_tokens, billed_tokens_for_prefix) * credit_rate. Credits appear as negative invoice lines and are reconciled monthly. They are not applied in real-time.

Attachment: sample_invoice_lines.pdf (PDF) — mapping of raw service calls -> suggested invoice line consolidation.
Attachment: kv_cache_crediting_chart.png (PNG) — illustration of typical weekly credit behavior.

If you'd like, Marissa can propose a conservative crediting language for the SOW / purchase order.

Cheers,

Hi Sarah — attaching the formal sample invoice lines and a short note you can forward to procurement. Below is the text we recommend pasting into your PR: 

--- recommended PR blurb for procurement ---
Redwood Inference billing: Tokens are metered per execution call. For pinned conversation_id usage, token usage is aggregated into a conversation bucket for reporting; the backend may split long contexts into multiple execution calls which appear as separate raw usage records but can be consolidated on the invoice as a single logical line upon request. KV cache/prefix reuse credits are applied monthly as invoice credits and are limited by the total billed tokens for the prefix during the crediting window. Rounding is applied to the configured billing quantum (example: 10-token quantum). Committed enterprise units replace standard floors and may include bespoke rounding and credit terms.
--- end blurb ---

Sample invoice lines included (attachment: sample_invoice_lines.pdf). For your procurement team, our recommended ask is to include a clause that allows Redwood to consolidate execution-level records into a single invoice line for pinned sessions to reduce accounting noise.

If Ornate would like a short clause: 
"Redwood Inference will provide consolidated billing lines for logical conversation windows upon customer request; Redwood's monthly invoice will include any applicable KV cache credits applied as separate credit line items."

Let me know and I can add this language to the SOW.

Thanks,
